paras: The assault on John H. Dorsey was an attack by a crowd on a Black man in Washington, D.C., on the afternoon of 17 March 1882. Three men named as members of the crowd were brought before the Police Court the next morning, where one was discharged and two were sentenced. The case drew only brief notices in two Washington evening papers.

According to the Evening Critic, Michael Long and Dan and Jerry Desmond "were in a crowd that assaulted a colored man named John H. Dorsey" on the afternoon of 17 March. Neither paper says where the assault took place, how many people were in the crowd, what led to it, or whether Dorsey was hurt.

On the morning of 18 March, Judge Snell of the Police Court dismissed the charge against Jerry Desmond. The Evening Star reported that Daniel Desmond, whose name it printed as "Dismond," and Michael Long were each "fined $5 or 15 days" on the charge of assaulting Dorsey. The Critic instead said the two men were sent to jail for fifteen days, which would follow if the fines went unpaid. No later report of the case was found.

Both papers treated the case as routine court news. The Critic gave it a single sentence among its "Laconic Locals," between notices of a mistrial and a church anniversary, and the Star listed it in its "Police Court Notes" beside the case of a woman sent to the workhouse for disorderly conduct. Each identified Dorsey only as "a colored man" and gave no race for the defendants, and neither offered comment on the attack.
